title: Observability data supplychain gap analysis and tactical runbook
body:
Summary:

This is a working analysis of the recent SLO burn incident (2025-11-04) where several downstream services reported elevated 99th percentile latencies and page noise while key telemetry streams were partially missing. The purpose is threefold: 1) capture on-call observations and quick mitigations, 2) draft a tactical runbook for similar supply-chain gaps in the telemetry pipeline, and 3) propose longer-term fixes and experiments to reduce pager noise and make SLO attribution faster.

Why this is different from the usual 'alert tuning' docs:
- Root cause appears upstream of alert evaluation: intermittent backlog and partial writes in the metric/log ingestion path (exporter agent restarts + transient disk pressure) caused repeated spikes in SLO burn alerts that were correlated but not caused by application error.
- We observed mixed signal semantics (half of traffic reported by proxy metrics, other half by application metrics), so naive alerting on any one signal created oscillations.
- This doc focuses on the telemetry "supply chain" (emit -> agent -> buffer -> aggregator -> storage -> evaluation) rather than only thresholds or debounce windows.

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 2025-11-04 02:38 UTC — Synthetic p95 latency starts rising in frontend-prod (alerts fired at 02:41).
- 02:42 — Multiple SLO burn alerts triggered for api-prod-route and embeddings-worker tiers. Oncall paged.
- 02:45 — SRE observes gaps in application-level request count metric (app.requests) where values drop to near-zero for short 30–90s windows. Proxy metrics (envoy.nginx.requests) show normal traffic.
- 02:48 — Telemetry agent logs on a subset of hosts show repeated 'write failed, retrying' messages and local buffer flushes due to transient disk throttle.
- 02:52 — Several aggregator scale-up events triggered but could not backfill missing points; alert suppression rules were not applied since the alerts are evaluated on the storage tier that receives partial writes.
- 03:10 — Agents stabilize after kernel oom/throttle resolved (root cause: node-level disk I/O contention due to a simultaneous backup job + slower ephemeral disk). Metrics slowly recovered; SLO burn alerts flapped as points reappeared.
- 03:30 — Incident declared mitigated; follow-ups opened.

Immediate mitigation steps taken (what worked):
1) Short-term evacuation: moved traffic off affected hosts using the service mesh weight shift (10% increments) to remove hosts with telemetry agent errors from rotation. Immediate reduction in SLO alerts.
2) Temporary alert mute: enabled a short (15m) global 'telemetry-ingestion-degraded' mute to avoid oncall exhaustion while engineers validated the pipeline state.
3) Restarted the exporter agents on impacted hosts after confirming disk pressure subsided; agents flushed buffered metrics.
4) Added a retroactive annotation to the storage index (time series) to mark the interval as 'partial-write' for downstream analysts.

Why alerts flapped and pagers were noisy (diagnosis):
- Asymmetric observability: alerts depended on different metric sources (app vs proxy). When app metrics dropped to zero for short intervals, SLO calculators interpreted it as zero successful requests and raised burn. Proxy metrics telling a different story created conflicting signal; engineers duplicated effort to decide which alert to trust.
- No upstream 'write success' signal: alert evaluation only checked end-state SLO; there was no automated gating that suppressed alerts if the ingestion layer reported degraded writes.
- Buffer replays created delayed datapoints: once agent recovered it replayed buffered points which changed the aggregated SLO windows, causing retrospective metric corrections and alert re-evaluation (flapping).

Tactical runbook (for oncall to follow when seeing similar symptoms):
TRIAGE CHECKLIST (first 10 minutes):
- Confirm user impact: check synthetic probes and error budgets across regions (synthetics are authoritative when telemetry ambiguous).
- Query two independent signals: proxy request rates and app-level success rates. If they diverge, suspect telemetry loss. (example queries in linked_artifacts)
- Check telemetry-agent health across hosts: `kubectl get pods -n telemetry -l app=exporter -o wide` and `kubectl logs` for 'retrying' or 'buffer flushed'.
- Look at aggregator ingress metrics (write_errors, accepted_batches) and storage write latencies. If write_errors > 0, mark incident as 'telemetry supply chain degraded'.
- If ingestion errors present, enable the 'telemetry-ingestion-degraded' silence for SLO burn alerts (owner: oncall SRE) to avoid noisy paging while investigating.
- If only a small subset of hosts affected, temporarily weight-shed them from traffic or add capacity.

RUNBOOK ACTIONS (escalation):
- Level 1 (oncall): triage, apply mutes, perform host-level restarts of exporter agent if disk pressure cleared. Document exact commands used in chat.
- Level 2 (sre lead): examine backup/cron job schedules; coordinate with infra-runbook to reschedule heavy I/O jobs. Consider live-migration or cordon of nodes if ephemeral disks are saturated.
- Level 3 (platform eng): implement short-term flag in aggregator to tag partial-write windows. This flag should be queryable by the alert evaluation engine to prevent firing on known ingestion gaps.

Quick queries and dashboards to run (examples):
- App request gap detection: count_over_time(app.requests[1m]) vs count_over_time(envoy.requests[1m]) — look for divergence > 25% sustained > 30s.
- Agent buffer queue length: telemetry.agent.buffer_size{host=~"prod.*"}
- Aggregator write_errors: sum(rate(aggregator.write_errors[1m])) by job

Mitigation timeline template to add to incident page:
- time, action, actor, result (include 'annotation id' for any storage tags).

Longer-term remediation proposals (owner suggestions included):
1) Upstream write-status signal (owner: telemetry infra) — implement a lightweight 'ingestion-health' metric emitted by the aggregator indicating percent of expected points received per minute. This should be used by SLO alerting as a gating signal.
2) Alert gating and attribution policy (owner: eng-sre/product-hosted-api) — modify SLO evaluation to prefer synthetic probes and proxy metrics for availability alerts, or to require multiple signals before paging.
3) Partial-write tagging (owner: telemetry infra) — add explicit interval tags when backfills occur so that retrospective corrections don't trigger pages; this is also useful for postmortem.
4) Disk pressure hardening (owner: platform-engineering) — reduce ephemeral disk reliance for exporter buffers; move to memory-backed circular queue + small persistent queue for durability, and adjust backup job time windows.
5) Sampling and cardinality controls (owner: telemetry infra + product teams) — reduce high-cardinality labels emitted by noisy libraries that exacerbate buffer sizes under load.
6) Synthetic probe expansion (owner: eng-dx) — increase probe coverage to act as a primary authoritative signal for availability SLOs so that telemetry gaps degrade alert severity rather than cause immediate pages.

Planned experiments (one-sentence descriptions):
- Experiment A: 'Gated page' — only escalate SLO alerts to page if ingestion-health >= 90% OR synthetic probe shows violation (2-week A/B).
- Experiment B: 'Buffered replay batching' — change agent replay behavior to emit a 'replay marker' event and suppress immediate alert re-evaluation for 10 minutes after large replay bursts.
- Experiment C: 'Adaptive debounce' — dynamic debounce windows tuned to ingestion latency distribution per service.

Open questions and unresolved items (for follow-up):
- What is the acceptable window to treat replayed points as historic (affects correction strategy)?
- How do we prevent silent data loss when agents drop buffered points permanently (need SLA around buffering guarantees)?
- Owner assignments for alert gating policy changes (need cross-team sign-off).

Notes to reviewers / next steps:
- Please add missing queries you used during the incident in the linked_artifacts section.
- Priya: can you scope the change to the evaluation engine to support an "ingestion-health" gating flag and estimate impact on alert latency?
- Platform-eng: provide a list of cron/backup jobs that could be rescheduled to avoid contention; prioritize changes that can be done without infra maintenance windows.

Appendix: example 'ingestion-health' metric semantics (proposal):
- metric name: telemetry.ingestion.expected_received_ratio
- semantics: fraction of expected points (based on proxy request counts + known emit rates) received by storage in the last 1m. If < 0.9, mark interval as 'partial-write'.
- usage: alert rules evaluate 'if SLO_violation AND ingestion_health >= 0.9 then page'.

Incident tags for search: telemetry-supplychain, ingestion-gap, replay-flap, disk-pressure, synthetic-probe-authority

End of draft — still needs: concrete query snippets, code pointers for agent logs, and owners to accept proposed changes.

(Internal scratch: remember to include timeline attachments + raw logs in the Confluence incident page and link JIRA OBS-1122 to the platform-engineering epic.)
